subject: Keystore rotation fix & customer coordination (short notice)
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: [ALERT] keystore rotation failures observed in prod (token issuance errors)

Team —

Monitoring started alerting at ~08:50PT: a subset of token requests are failing during keystore lookup after a recent maintenance on the vault cluster (node zk-3). Error pattern: AES key lookup returns a 500 during rotation window which surface as 401s downstream for short-lived tokens. The bulk of affected requests are in the us-west region; we estimate ~0.7% of requests are impacted and concentrated on model-serving routes with high qps.

Immediate notes:
- Root cause hypothesis: race between rotation job and stale cache invalidation, leading to KV descriptor mismatch.
- Impact: token issuance failures, transient 401s; degraded experience for a small subset of customers.
- Current mitigation: we disabled the rotation job at 09:05PT and backfilled last-good keys to the in-memory cache. Errors decreased but not fully resolved — some services still attempt one-time key exchange and get 500s.

I pushed a code-side short patch to add a guarded fallback to use previous key if lookup fails (attached). It requires a rolling redeploy to the inference frontends and a coordinated keystore restart on the vault nodes. Given risk to token issuance, I recommend a short-notice maintenance window and proactive customer notification.

Attachments: keystore_patch_v1.tar.gz (patch), keystore_fix_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook)

Questions:
1) Can infra run the rolling redeploy on the frontend fleet (canary -> bulk) with a 20m window?
2) Should we notify affected customers now with opt-in for immediate restart, or wait for the patch to be deployed internally first?

-naomi
Naomi Feldman
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.park@acme-retail.com, ops@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2029 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] keystore rotation failures observed in prod (token issuance errors)

Thanks Naomi —

Connor / Marcus: please confirm capacity for a rolling redeploy starting at 10:00PT (canary -> 30m observation -> bulk). We want to minimize customer impact; canary should include low-latency tenants only.

Jordan / Acme Ops: we’re preparing a short maintenance to address a keystore rotation edge-case that’s causing token issuance failures for a subset of requests. We expect the total window to be ~20–30 minutes for frontends + a short service restart on our vault cluster. If you rely on uninterrupted token issuance during that period and cannot tolerate a short interruption, reply with "opt-out" and we'll schedule a dedicated maintenance window. Otherwise no action required on your side; we’ll send a follow-up with exact timing in the next 30 minutes.

Action items assigned:
- Naomi: finalize runbook and cut release (09:35)
- Connor: confirm canary group and redeploy start time (09:40)
- Marcus: prepare incident channel and postmortem template (09:45)

-Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2029 09:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] keystore rotation failures observed in prod (token issuance errors)

We can run the rolling redeploy starting 10:10PT. Canary will be ~5% of frontend capacity: low-qps tenants + internal traffic. If canary looks good for 20m we’ll push to the rest in 3 waves with ~7m between waves to ensure caches rehydrate and we don’t trigger the rotation concurrently.

Notes: we’ll set circuit-breaker thresholds and fail-open for non-critical routes to avoid bulk 401 storms. Naomi — please confirm the guard clause behavior in the patch: if the lookup fails it returns the previous key for 3 minutes before re-raising error; is that correct? Also, provide the exact service restart command for the vault nodes to include in the runbook.

-Connor
Sr. Infra Engineer

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.park@acme-retail.com, ops@acme-retail.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2029 09:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] keystore rotation failures observed in prod (token issuance errors)

Connor — yes. Patch behavior: fallback to previous key for 180s if the new key lookup returns 5xx. Patch increments the in-memory key TTL to allow queues to drain. Service restart for vault is: sudo systemctl restart redwood-vault; check kv-sync status: /usr/local/bin/kv-sync status --health. Full runbook attached (keystore_fix_runbook_v1.pdf).

Jordan / Acme — we’re aiming to start the redeploy at 10:10PT and expect the end-to-end customer-visible window to be ~20m. We will send a final heads-up at 09:55PT with exact timing and will post updates to the incident channel.

-Naomi
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Park <jordan.park@acme-retail.com>, Ops Team <ops@acme-retail.com>, procurement@acme-retail.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2029 09:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Short-notice maintenance: keystore rotation fix (10:10PT start)

Jordan —

Quick update and what we need from you:

What’s happening
- We identified an edge-case in our keystore rotation that can cause token issuance to fail briefly for a subset of requests. We’ll be applying a short patch and performing a rolling redeploy + brief restart on a small set of keystore nodes to fully clear the condition.

Schedule
- Start: 10:10PT today
- Expected customer-visible window: 20 minutes (we’ll run a canary for 20 minutes and then roll the remainder in waves)

Customer impact
- Some requests may see transient 401s for up to 3 minutes while caches rehydrate. Most customers will not be affected.

Your options
- No action: we’ll proceed at 10:10PT and handle the update automatically.
- Opt-out: reply to this email with "opt-out" and we will schedule a dedicated maintenance window at a later date.

We apologize for the short notice. If you need a phone bridge, let us know and we’ll spin one up. We’ll also share a postmortem and the runbook after the incident.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
